An example CNN is shown in Fig. 1. The ﬁrst layer of a neural network takes the original data (e.g. an X-Ray image) as the input, and each subsequent layer computes a function over the previous output. A CNN processes the input with a sequence of layers and outputs a result vector (called logits), which demonstrates the relative weights of different potential classes. The class with the largest weight is the target class. In most situations, we will use softmax function to convert the logits to a probability vector, each element of which shows the probability that the input is classiﬁed into a certain class. Below we describe the clean abstractions of each layer. Convolutional Layer (Conv). The input to a convolutional layer is a w × h × c image where w and h are the width and height of the image and c is the number of channels, e.g. an RGB image has c = 3. The convolutional layer has k ﬁlters (or kernels) of size f w × f h × c . In a convolutional layer, an input image is convolved in turn with k ﬁlters, and thus producing k output images.
